To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the spatial and angular shifts are asymmetric with respect to the direction of the incident wave and the direction of the wave reflected (or transmitted) from the crystal, and that they depend on the sign of the magnetic permeability of the crystal.
the spatial and angular shifts of the reflected and transmitted waves, as well as the spatial shift of the reflected waves, depend on the polarization of the incident waves.

the first-order nonspecular effect emerges in the plane of the layers for both the reflected and transmitted waves for a quasi-plane wave of the TM or TE type normally incident from the outside on a finite magnetic photonic crystal having a normal magnetic polariton spectrum, asymmetrical with regard to the inversion of wave propagation direction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the nonspecular effects that occur as a quasi-plane wave passes through a finite photonic crystal with an asymmetric spectrum of magnetic polaritons.
a new type of nonspecular effect that occurs as a quasi-plane wave passes through a finite one-dimensional photonic crystal.
the study of the nonspecular effects of a quasi-plane wave passing through a finite one-dimensional photonic crystal with an asymmetric polariton spectrum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the nonspecular effects that occur as a quasi-plane wave passes through a finite photonic crystal with an asymmetric polariton spectrum are caused by a change in the phase of the reflected and transmitted waves, which is associated with the presence of a finite photonic structure.
the first order nonspecular effects are not observed for quasi-plane waves incident from outside on finite one-dimensional magnetic crystals with an asymmetric polariton spectrum.

the Goos-Hänchen and Imbert–Fedorov effects, and the related phenomena of the lateral shift and angular shift of light, are the result of the nonspecular nature of the reflection and refraction of light, which in turn is due to the wave nature of light and the diffraction of light by the boundaries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the first-order nonspecular effect for the reflected and transmitted quasi-plane waves (particularly the angular Goos– Hanchen effect) is possible in a finite one-dimensional photonic crystal with an asymmetric magnetic polariton spectrum.

the first-order spatial and angular Goös-Hänchen effect, as well as the first-order spatial Goös-Hänchenn effect in the plane of the layers, are observed for a quasi-plane wave of a TM (TE) type, normally incident from outside, on a finite one dimensional magnetic photonic crystal, with a spectrum of magnetic normal polaritons asymmetric with respect to the direction of wave motion inversion.

we have demonstrated the existence of first-order nonspecular reflection and transmission effects that are due to the presence of an asymmetric spectrum of normal magnetic (or electric) polaritons in a finite photonic crystal with magnetic (or electric permittivity) and magnetic (or electric permeability) layers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the asymmetry of the polariton spectrum leads to an asymmetry of the reflection and transmission coefficients, which, in turn, leads to the occurrence of the first-order nonspecular effect.

the Goos–Henchen effect is not a purely local effect and that the Goos-Hanchen shift is determined not only by the local value of the refractive index, but also by the local value and the spatial distribution of the derivative of the refractive-index profile.
the spatial and angular shift of a wave reflected by the photonic crystal depends not only on the angle of incidence, but also on the direction of propagation of the incident wave.
